items.title: dell-5530 maintenance window: rotate leaked node token, re-parent orphaned Scheduled Task, decide auto-logon
items.description: One window closes three things at once. The node token was exposed in a transcript on 2026-09-09 and is still live (risk bounded to LAN: agent binds 192.168.1.250:8790, node not on tailnet). The agent is ALSO orphaned from its Scheduled Task (task state Ready, LastTaskResult 0x8007042B) so Stop-ScheduledTask is a no-op and RestartOnFailure gives no auto-restart. Costs all 6 ConPTY sessions - they are in-process children of the agent and cannot survive a restart by design. Runbook is in the multi-node memory note.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot sessions + each running claude's transcript id before shutdown
Graceful POST /v1/internal/shutdown (schtasks /end is a no-op on the orphan)

Start-ScheduledTask; task state shows Running and tracks the live agent
Old token returns 401, new token 200, verified from the node side
Decide BootTrigger vs LogonType=InteractiveToken (auto-logon) - do NOT switch to S4U without checking the show_on_desktop ConPTY path
Sessions recreated and claude --resume'd per snapshot

items.title: Rate-limit / lockout on node-agent bearer auth
items.description: Token comparison is constant-time but unbounded: an attacker on the LAN (or on any network a node is exposed to) can attempt tokens indefinitely. Found in the 2026-09-09 internet-connectivity audit.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated 401s from one source are throttled or locked out
Legitimate heartbeat traffic (20s interval) is never throttled
Lockout state cannot wedge a node permanently

items.title: Node token rotation and revocation mechanism
items.description: There is no rotation/revocation path today - rotating a token is a manual, per-node, restart-requiring edit of two files (proven twice on 2026-09-09: macbook rotated, dell-5530 deferred because its restart costs 6 sessions). Roadmap Phase 5 names this.
acceptance_criteria: A token can be rotated without hand-editing files on both sides
Revocation takes effect without a full node restart, or the restart cost is documented per platform
Old token is provably rejected afterwards

notes: AC1 (rotate without hand-editing both sides) MET: POST /dashboard/api/nodes/{id}/token/rotate stages a replacement; the node collects it on its next heartbeat via /token/refresh and adopts it in memory; the controller moves its own outbound copy (token file + env var + live RemoteNodeClient) only once a heartbeat arrives signed with the new token. Operator never sees a token.

AC2 (revocation without a full node restart) MET: enforced controller-side at the one shared _verify_node_token site, so it takes effect on the node's next request on every platform with zero node-side action; outbound is cleared at the same time. Per-platform cost table in docs/node-token-rotation.md.
AC3 (old token provably rejected) MET: confirmation REVOKES the superseded token rather than letting it expire; asserted at the route (401 + verdict=REVOKED) and in the store.
Grace is open-ended by default (closed by confirmation, not a clock) so a node offline during rotation is never locked out; grace_seconds=0 gives an immediate cutover for a compromised token.
Backward compatible: nodes with no credential record keep using the legacy env-var path; newly enrolled nodes are adopted automatically, so they are rotatable from their first heartbeat.

Staging measurement note: POST /dashboard/api/node/test-connection cannot verify an outbound TOKEN -- the agent's /v1/health is an unauthenticated liveness probe by design. Use /dashboard/api/nodes/{id}/refresh-capabilities for that. Documented in the staging README.

A remote upgrade through the agent's own API was rejected as unsafe: restarting it would mean POST /v1/internal/shutdown and trusting an unverified Restart=always, and if that assumption is wrong the node goes dark with no way back in.

Observation, not yet attributed: 2 heartbeat 500s and 3 'database is locked' errors in node_registry.heartbeat, all within the single second 03:03:00, during the burst around the dell-linux agent restart. Zero in the preceding 24h and zero since (18 consecutive 200s in the following 2 min). nodes.db already uses WAL with a 10s busy timeout, so something held its write lock for >10s; the rotation code touches a different database (node-credentials.db) and is not an obvious cause. Worth watching rather than assuming either way.

items.title: Internet node transport: outbound WSS node->controller (roadmap Phase 2)
items.description: The 2026-09-09 audit's core finding: the data plane is controller->node (inbound to the node), so a NAT'd node is visible-but-uncontrollable - heartbeat lands, dashboard shows ONLINE, every real operation fails. Overlay VPN (now unblocked) is a workaround, not a fix; outbound WSS removes the inbound requirement entirely and is the only option that scales past hand-configured peers.
acceptance_criteria: A node behind NAT with no inbound port is fully controllable
Reconnect/backoff across sleep, Wi-Fi change and IP change without manual re-registration
Tasks enqueued while offline auto-dispatch on reconnect with no duplicates

notes: 2026-09-14 staging E2E on 8777 (own state dir, production untouched). AC3 MET: replay of a consumed code -> HTTP 401 ENROLLMENT_ALREADY_USED, unknown code -> ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND, both with an identical `detail` string so the two are indistinguishable to a caller; audit rows node_enrolled (node_id set) and node_enrollment_rejected (node_id None) written per attempt. items.title: Rapid Capture Inbox + Parallel Planner Pool for Work mode
items.description:
FEATURE: Rapid Capture Inbox + Parallel Planner Pool for Work mode.
(Requirement preserved VERBATIM from the user, 2026-09-13. Do NOT duplicate the
existing Knowledge Map / Runbook registry / Bug Planner / token policy /
WORK_POLICY work -- build on those.)

Goal: the human developer can dump issues/ideas much faster than one planner can
deeply analyze them. Capture must stay fast, while planning/execution happen
independently and in parallel.

1) RAPID CAPTURE INBOX
- Accept one issue or a batch of many issues in one message.
- Split batch into atomic work items without requiring deep analysis first.
- Capture only lightweight metadata initially: issue_id, project, raw_text,
  short_title, rough_type, likely_module(optional), rough_difficulty(optional),
  created_at, source, priority, duplicate_candidate.
- Capture must never block on root-cause analysis.
- Return concise acknowledgement/count/state rather than a long analysis.

2) PER-ISSUE STATE MACHINE (durable across restart)
NEW -> TRIAGED -> PLANNING -> READY -> EXECUTING -> PREVIEW_READY -> VERIFYING -> DONE
Side states: NEEDS_USER_HINT, NEEDS_REDEFINE, BLOCKED, DUPLICATE, CANCELLED, FAILED

3) PARALLEL PLANNER POOL
- N planning jobs concurrently instead of a single global planner bottleneck.
- Each planner gets only one issue + relevant project policy + targeted
  Knowledge Map context.
- Planner produces the existing Bug Execution Spec contract.
- Must respect difficulty triage / token policy / spec completeness rules.
- Concurrency configurable globally and per project.
- Avoid double-planning the same issue: claim/lease/lock semantics.

4) NEEDS_USER_HINT
- For genuinely difficult/ambiguous bugs, planner first performs bounded
  analysis and formulates at most 1-3 precise high-value questions.
- Do not block other issues while waiting.
- Preserve all prior analysis/spec draft.
- When the developer answers, attach HUMAN_HINTS and resume the SAME issue,
  not a new task.
- User hint is guidance; current code remains source of truth.

5) BATCH SPLITTING
- A 20-bullet input becomes multiple atomic work items.
- Detect obvious dependencies/duplicates.
- Preserve original batch/source linkage.
- Do not over-split one coherent bug into meaningless microtasks.
- Allow later merge/split correction.

6) EXECUTION SESSION CREATION
- Do NOT create a tmux/agent session per captured issue immediately.
- Capture and planning are lightweight state/jobs.
- Create a worker/session only when an issue reaches READY/EXECUTING and
  capacity is available.
- Suggested naming: <project>-work-<issue_id> when a real session is needed.

7) QUEUE/DASHBOARD UX
- Work-mode view with counts and compact cards/rows for: Inbox / Planning /
  Needs User Hint / Ready / Executing / Preview Ready / Done / Failed.
- Each issue shows: issue id, title, project/module, difficulty, state,
  planner/worker, age, dependencies, last update.
- Filtering and bulk priority change.
- A Rapid Capture box accepting many pasted bullets at once.

8) BACKPRESSURE / FAIRNESS
- Configurable planner concurrency and worker concurrency.
- Priority + FIFO within the same priority.
- Prevent one project or one huge bug from starving all others.
- Planning may continue while worker capacity is full.
- Never spawn unbounded sessions.

9) DUPLICATE/SIMILAR ISSUE HANDLING
- Before expensive planning, use the existing similar-bug retrieval /
  fingerprint (terminal_mcp/context_pack.py).
- Mark possible duplicates and reuse history/spec where safe.
- Never silently drop distinct issues.

10) API/CLI
- Stable backend primitives: capture_issue(s), list/filter issues, claim
  planning job, attach_user_hint, resume issue, update priority/state,
  concise queue summary. CLI desirable; backend contract first.

11) POLICY INTEGRATION
- Auto-load canonical WORK_POLICY; record policy_version/policy_hash per
  issue and per planning attempt (terminal_mcp/work_policy.py).
- Reuse Knowledge Map, Bug Planner, Runbooks, token telemetry -- no parallel
  duplicate systems.
- Normal non-work terminal sessions remain backward compatible.

12) OBSERVABILITY
- Track: capture latency, planning wait time, planning duration,
  NEEDS_USER_HINT count, READY wait time, execution duration, duplicate reuse,
  planner concurrency, worker concurrency.
- Concise logs on success; detailed logs only on failure.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS
A. Paste 10 distinct bullet issues -> 10 persistent items captured quickly;
   capture does not wait for deep analysis.
B. planner concurrency=3 -> three different items PLANNING simultaneously with
   no duplicate claim.
C. One hard issue moves to NEEDS_USER_HINT with <=3 precise questions while
   other issues keep planning/executing.
D. Answering the hint resumes the SAME issue with the prior draft preserved.
E. Worker capacity=2 never creates more than two execution workers even with
   20 READY items.
F. Restart terminal-mcp: inbox/state/claims recover; stale claims reclaimable.
G. A batch containing a duplicate flags/reuses it instead of blindly re-planning.
H. Normal terminal sessions unaffected.
I. No secrets persisted in issue metadata/spec/history.

IMPLEMENTATION PRIORITY
persistent issue/state model + capture API + planner claims/concurrency +
user-hint resume  ->  execution spawning/backpressure  ->  UI polish/telemetry.

BUILD ON (do not duplicate):
- terminal_mcp/bug_spec.py        (spec contract, triage, budgets, assist)
- terminal_mcp/context_pack.py    (similar-bug retrieval, fingerprint buckets)
- terminal_mcp/project_knowledge.py (knowledge map + confidence)
- terminal_mcp/procedures.py      (runbook registry)
- terminal_mcp/work_policy.py     (canonical policy + bindings)
- terminal_mcp/work_telemetry.py  (honest token provenance)
- terminal_mcp/work_store.py / work_service.py / queue_engine.py (existing queue)

STANDING CONSTRAINTS: never restart node-agents; no reboot; never kill live
tmux/ConPTY sessions; never bypass Cloudflare Access/Tailscale; never read or
print secrets; announce before restarting the controller (cách 1).
acceptance_criteria: A. 10 pasted bullets -> 10 persistent items, capture does not wait for analysis
B. planner concurrency=3 -> 3 items PLANNING at once, no duplicate claim
C. hard issue -> NEEDS_USER_HINT with <=3 precise questions, others continue
D. answering a hint resumes the SAME issue with prior draft preserved
E. worker capacity=2 never creates more than 2 execution workers
F. restart: inbox/state/claims recover; stale claims reclaimable
G. duplicate in a batch is flagged/reused, not blindly re-planned
H. normal terminal sessions unaffected
I. no secrets persisted in issue metadata/spec/history

- Task<->worktree link: queue_tasks.metadata JSON -> metadata.git_isolation
  {repo_path, branch, base_sha, worktree_path} and metadata.expected_cwd. Written by
  git_isolation_service.create_isolated_task. A worktree with no such task is an ORPHAN.
- Task state: queue_tasks.status. The ONLY mutation path is
  queue_store._transition_locked (called by transition_task); it already writes a
  queue_events row in the same transaction. This is the minimal chokepoint for any
  lifecycle hook.
- Session -> path usage: session_registry SessionRecord(node_id, session_name, cwd,
  repo_root, status). Node-scoped; the controller cannot stat a remote node's paths.
- Node reachability/execution: node_client NodeClient protocol (LocalNodeClient /
  RemoteNodeClient) + node_agent HTTP routes.
- Repo state evidence: coordinator.git_repo_evidence / node_aware_repo_evidence (fails
  closed: RepoEvidenceError for a real repo problem, RepoEvidenceUnavailable for "could
  not look").
- Audit: audit.AuditStore.record(action=, session=, result=, reason=, actor=, node_id=,
  latency_ms=, policy_source=). Never put file content in it.
- Events: event_bus.EventBus.publish(type=, entity_type=, entity_id=, payload=,
  idempotency_key=). New types MUST be added to KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES.
- Config: config.AppConfig + a new frozen dataclass section and a _load_*_config validator
  that raises ValueError on out-of-range input (never silently clamps).

STATE MODEL (new, on the task's own metadata -- see P1):
metadata.worktree_cleanup = {state, classified_at, eligible_at, policy, reasons[],
attempts, last_error, removed_at, reclaimed_bytes, evidence{...}}
states: NONE -> CLEANUP_PENDING -> CLEANUP_ELIGIBLE -> CLEANUP_DONE
                              \-> CLEANUP_REVIEW -> (human) -> CLEANUP_ELIGIBLE | CLEANUP_ABANDONED
                              \-> CLEANUP_BLOCKED (terminal until re-classified)
CLEANUP_PENDING is entered when the task reaches a cleanup-eligible lifecycle state.
CLEANUP_ELIGIBLE only after grace elapsed AND classification == AUTO_SAFE.

CRITICAL CORRECTION FOUND IN AUDIT: there is NO 'FAILED_FINAL' status anywhere.
queue_store.TERMINAL_STATUSES == (COMPLETED, SKIPPED, CANCELLED); FAILED and BLOCKED are
explicitly NOT terminal (terminal_queue_retry/skip/cancel still apply). work_store
TERMINAL_WORK_STATES == (COMPLETE, CANCELLED). Therefore the cleanup trigger predicate is:
  status in (COMPLETED, SKIPPED, CANCELLED)
  OR (status == FAILED AND attempt_count >= max_attempts)
A bare FAILED must NEVER trigger cleanup -- it is retryable and the worktree is the retry's
working directory.

POLICY CLASSES (fail-closed):
- AUTO_SAFE: every predicate below proven true. Only this class may be auto-removed.
- REVIEW: safe to keep, needs a human. Any predicate that could not be EVALUATED
  (node offline, evidence stale, git error, permission denied, detached HEAD) lands here.
- BLOCKED: actively dangerous to remove (dirty, unmerged-and-unpushed, valuable ignored
  data, process/session/service using it, main worktree, path outside allowlist).
Unknown ALWAYS degrades toward REVIEW/BLOCKED, never toward AUTO_SAFE.

AUTO_SAFE PREDICATE (all must hold, each with recorded evidence):
1. NOT the main worktree: `git rev-parse --git-dir` != `--git-common-dir` inside the
   candidate (verified primitive). Refuse if equal. Also refuse if worktree_path equals
   any configured repo root.
2. Path allowlisted: worktree_path resolves (symlinks followed BEFORE the check) inside
   config allowed roots, and is not a symlink itself, not a mount point, not a bind mount.
3. CLEAN: `git status --porcelain` empty.
4. MERGED or PRESERVED:
   merged  = `git merge-base --is-ancestor <worktree_head> <integration_ref>` (default main)
   preserved = the branch tip exists on a remote AND <worktree_head> is an ancestor of that
   remote ref. Pushed-but-not-merged counts as PRESERVED (work is not lost) but is
   classified REVIEW by default, promoted to AUTO_SAFE only when
   config.allow_preserved_unmerged is true.
   Detached HEAD => no branch identity => REVIEW, never AUTO_SAFE.
5. NO LIVE REFERENCES (evaluated ON the owning node):
   - no process with cwd inside the path (Linux: readlink /proc/*/cwd)
   - no tmux pane with pane_current_path inside the path
   - no session_registry record (any non-DELETED status) whose cwd/repo_root is inside it
   - no systemd unit WorkingDirectory inside it
   - no container/bind mount referencing it (/proc/mounts scan)
   Any positive match => BLOCKED. Inability to check => REVIEW.
6. NO VALUABLE IGNORED DATA: `git status --porcelain --ignored=matching` -> '!!' entries.
   Classify each: SAFE_CACHE (__pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, node_modules,
   dist, build, .venv, *.pyc) vs VALUABLE (*.db, *.sqlite*, .env*, *.pem, *.key, *credentials*,
   node-agent.env, evidence/, *.log above config threshold, anything matching
   repo_read.SECRET_PATH_GLOBS). Any VALUABLE entry => BLOCKED with the paths listed
   (paths only -- NEVER contents).
7. REPO EVIDENCE FRESH: evidence collected at decision time on the owning node, age <=
   config.max_evidence_age_seconds. Stale/unavailable => REVIEW.
8. GRACE ELAPSED: now >= terminal_transition_at + grace_seconds.
9. LOCK HELD: a ResourceLockStore lock namespaced 'worktree_janitor:<node_id>:<worktree_path>'
   is held for the whole classify+remove sequence.

HARD INVARIANTS (must be expressed as tests, not comments):
I1. The janitor NEVER passes force=True / --force to git worktree remove. Not under disk
    pressure, not on retry, not ever. git_worktree.remove_worktree(force=...) must be called
    with force=False from every janitor path.
I2. The main worktree and any configured repo root can never be selected.
I3. A dirty or unmerged-and-unpushed worktree is never removed, regardless of disk pressure.
I4. The controller never removes a path on another node (no os/shutil/subprocess rm against
    a remote path). Remote removal happens only via the owning node-agent endpoint.
I5. Classification is pure/read-only and has no side effects other than audit+events.
I6. Every removal writes an audit row with reclaimed bytes and the full evidence set BEFORE
    the removal is attempted and a result row after.
I7. Disk pressure may only shorten grace (down to a configured floor) and reorder
    candidates. It may never downgrade a predicate, promote REVIEW/BLOCKED, or enable force.
I8. Feature flag default is observe_only; nothing is ever removed until an operator opts in.

DANGEROUS FAILURE MODES (each needs a named test):
F1. Deleting a worktree a retry still needs (bare FAILED treated as final).
F2. Deleting unmerged work that exists nowhere else (branch only local, not merged).
F3. Deleting an ignored-but-valuable file (a task's sqlite db, .env, collected evidence).
F4. Controller running rm against a path that only exists on another node -- deleting the
    CONTROLLER's like-named directory.
F5. Two janitors racing on one worktree (double remove, or remove during another's classify).
F6. Crash between `git worktree remove` and the metadata write -> state says PENDING while
    the directory is gone. Recovery must be idempotent and converge to CLEANUP_DONE.
F7. Stale admin entry (directory gone, git still lists it) treated as a live worktree, or
    `git worktree prune` run while another worktree is mid-creation.
F8. Root-owned or permission-denied artifacts inside the tree -> partial removal leaving a
    half-deleted worktree. Must be detected and left BLOCKED, never retried with force.
F9. Windows locked directory -> remove fails; must not retry-loop or force.
F10. Symlink/mount/bind-mount escape: worktree_path containing a symlink to a real repo.
F11. Evidence staleness: classifying AUTO_SAFE on evidence collected minutes ago after a
     human started working in the tree.
F12. Task reopen/retry after CLEANUP_DONE -> must fail loudly (worktree gone) rather than
     silently recreating and losing the link.
F13. Parent/child (planner split) -- a parent's worktree removed while a child still works
     in it, or a child's removal attributed to the parent.

items.description:

- classify(candidate, policy, evidence, refs) -> {policy_class, reasons[], evidence{},

items.title: Worktree Janitor P1: cleanup lifecycle state set from queue_store's single chokepoint
items.description:
Record cleanup lifecycle state on the task, and set it from the ONE chokepoint.

Hook site: queue_store._transition_locked (the only place a task's status ever changes;
it already writes a queue_events row in the same transaction). Do NOT hook
QueueService.on_completed or QueueEngine.on_completed -- audited: there are TWO call sites
(queue_service.py:658 and queue_engine.py:515), so neither is a chokepoint and a task
completed via the other path would silently never be marked.

Trigger predicate (exactly this, per the contract -- FAILED_FINAL does not exist):
  to_status in (COMPLETED, SKIPPED, CANCELLED)
  OR (to_status == FAILED AND attempt_count >= max_attempts)
AND the task has metadata.git_isolation.worktree_path.
Effect: set metadata.worktree_cleanup = {state: CLEANUP_PENDING, classified_at: null,
eligible_at: <now + grace_seconds>, policy: null, reasons: [], attempts: 0}. Idempotent:
re-entering a terminal state never resets an existing record or bumps attempts.

Schema: metadata is already a JSON TEXT column -- prefer writing inside it (no migration).
If a queryable index is needed for the periodic sweep, add it as a tracked
Migration(N, ...) appended to QUEUE_MIGRATIONS (schema.py/apply_migrations), never a bare
ALTER TABLE.

Events: add WORKTREE_CLEANUP_PENDING, WORKTREE_CLEANUP_ELIGIBLE, WORKTREE_CLEANUP_REVIEW,
WORKTREE_CLEANUP_BLOCKED, WORKTREE_CLEANUP_DONE, WORKTREE_CLEANUP_FAILED to
event_bus.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES and publish with entity_type='worktree',
entity_id=worktree_path, idempotency_key=<task_id>:<state> so a retried producer cannot
duplicate.

Reopen/retry (F12): if a task leaves a terminal state (retry/reopen) while
worktree_cleanup.state is PENDING/REVIEW, clear the record. If state is DONE, the worktree
is gone -- the existing Coordinator expected_cwd gate must refuse dispatch with a clear
reason (WORKTREE_REMOVED) rather than silently proceeding; add that reason, do not weaken
the gate.

DoD: tests that a COMPLETED/SKIPPED/CANCELLED isolated task gets CLEANUP_PENDING with the
right eligible_at; a bare FAILED does NOT; FAILED at max_attempts DOES; a non-isolated task
never gets the record; the hook is idempotent across repeated transitions; a retry clears
PENDING; a retry after DONE is refused by the gate with WORKTREE_REMOVED. Backward
compatible: an existing task with no worktree_cleanup key behaves exactly as today.
acceptance_criteria: The hook lives in queue_store._transition_locked, NOT on QueueService/QueueEngine.on_completed (two call sites, not a chokepoint)
CLEANUP_PENDING is set for COMPLETED/SKIPPED/CANCELLED and for FAILED at max_attempts; never for bare FAILED; never for a non-isolated task
The hook is idempotent and never resets an existing record or bumps attempts
New WORKTREE_CLEANUP_* types added to event_bus.KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES and published with an idempotency_key
A retry/reopen clears a PENDING/REVIEW record; a dispatch after CLEANUP_DONE is refused by the existing expected_cwd gate with reason WORKTREE_REMOVED
Any schema change is a tracked Migration appended to QUEUE_MIGRATIONS, never a bare ALTER TABLE
A task with no worktree_cleanup key behaves exactly as before (backward compatible)

items.title: Worktree Janitor P2: local safe executor (never --force, lock + audit + fresh evidence)
items.description:
Local safe executor. The first task that may delete anything.

New: worktree_janitor.execute(candidate, policy_result, *, dry_run) in the same module,
plus WorktreeJanitorService (terminal_mcp/worktree_janitor_service.py) wiring engine ->
lock -> audit -> events -> git_worktree.remove_worktree.

Rules (non-negotiable, each a test):
- Only acts on policy_class == AUTO_SAFE, and RE-CLASSIFIES immediately before removal with
  FRESH evidence while holding the lock. A candidate that was AUTO_SAFE at scan time and is
  no longer must abort with EVIDENCE_CHANGED and no removal.
- Calls git_worktree.remove_worktree(repo_path, worktree_path, force=False) ALWAYS. Never
  force=True. Never shutil.rmtree. If git refuses (WORKTREE_DIRTY /
  WORKTREE_REMOVE_FAILED), record BLOCKED with the git stderr and stop -- no fallback,
  no retry with force.
- Lock: ResourceLockStore key 'worktree_janitor:<node_id>:<worktree_path>' held across
  classify+remove; LOCK_UNAVAILABLE => skip this candidate this run (never wait long).
- Audit: one row BEFORE (action='worktree_cleanup_attempt', full evidence + predicted
  reclaimed_bytes) and one AFTER (action='worktree_cleanup_result', result=OK/DENIED/FAILED,
  reclaimed_bytes actually observed, latency_ms). Paths and sizes only -- never file content.
- Metadata: on success set state=CLEANUP_DONE, removed_at, reclaimed_bytes. On refusal set
  CLEANUP_BLOCKED + reasons. On transient failure increment attempts and keep PENDING, with
  a configured max_attempts after which it becomes REVIEW (never an infinite retry loop).
- Crash recovery (F6): the sequence must be idempotent. If the directory is already gone but
  metadata says PENDING, converge to CLEANUP_DONE and run `git worktree prune` for that repo.
  Run prune ONLY after a successful removal or when a stale admin entry was positively
  identified -- never speculatively while another worktree may be mid-creation (F7).
- dry_run=True is the default for the MCP tool.

MCP tools: terminal_worktree_janitor_run_once(repo_path='', node='', dry_run=True,
limit=10) and terminal_worktree_janitor_review(worktree_path, decision=approve|abandon,
actor) for REVIEW items. run_once refuses to remove anything unless
config mode == auto_execute AND dry_run=False.

DoD: real-git tests -- AUTO_SAFE clean+merged worktree is removed and reclaimed_bytes > 0;
dirty tree is never removed even with disk pressure simulated; force is never passed
(assert on the git_worktree call args); a candidate that turns dirty between scan and
execute aborts; concurrent janitors (two threads) result in exactly one removal;
already-removed directory converges to DONE idempotently; a permission-denied subtree
leaves BLOCKED with no partial state; audit rows contain no file content.
acceptance_criteria: Removal only for AUTO_SAFE, and only after re-classifying with fresh evidence while holding the lock; EVIDENCE_CHANGED aborts with no removal
git_worktree.remove_worktree is always called with force=False; a test asserts the call arguments and that no force path exists
A dirty worktree is not removed even with disk pressure simulated at 99% full
ResourceLockStore lock namespaced worktree_janitor:<node_id>:<worktree_path>; two concurrent janitors produce exactly one removal
An audit row is written before the attempt and after the result, with reclaimed bytes and evidence, and contains no file content
An already-removed directory converges idempotently to CLEANUP_DONE; git worktree prune runs only after a real removal or a positively-identified stale admin entry
Transient failures are bounded by max_attempts then become REVIEW; a permission-denied subtree leaves BLOCKED with no partial state
dry_run defaults to True and nothing is removed unless mode == auto_execute and dry_run=False

items.title: Worktree Janitor P3: periodic sweep for orphans and post-crash stale state
items.description:
Periodic janitor service: catch orphans and stale state after crash/reboot.

Follow the established loop shape EXACTLY (maintenance.py / queue_loop.py / fleet_loop.py):
daemon thread + threading.Event stop + run_once() + start()/stop()/is_alive(), constructed
in server_http.py and started ONLY if its config flag is enabled. run_once() must remain
callable via MCP even when the loop is off (the project's standing 'manual always
available, only the automatic trigger is gated' posture).

Sweep responsibilities:
- Enumerate every known repo root (from session_registry repo_root values + configured
  roots), list worktrees, classify all.
- ORPHANS: a worktree whose worktree_path matches no task metadata (registry lost, task
  pruned, created outside the isolation service). Never AUTO_SAFE on the first sighting:
  require it to be seen orphaned in >= orphan_confirm_runs consecutive runs
  (default 2) AND older than orphan_min_age_seconds, then classify normally. A brand-new
  worktree mid-creation must never be swept (F7).
- STALE CLEANUP STATE: tasks with worktree_cleanup.state == PENDING whose eligible_at has
  passed -> classify and (if mode allows) execute. Tasks whose directory is gone -> converge
  to DONE.
- STALE ADMIN ENTRIES: worktrees git lists whose directory is absent -> prune, per P2 rules.
- Bounded: max_candidates_per_run, per-run wall-clock budget, and it must never block
  startup or hold a lock across the whole sweep.

Config: add interval_seconds (default 900), orphan_confirm_runs, orphan_min_age_seconds to
WorktreeJanitorConfig. Loop enabled flag separate from mode so an operator can run the
sweep in observe_only.

DoD: tests that the loop is not started when disabled; run_once works with the loop off;
an orphan is not actioned on first sighting but is on the Nth; a worktree created 10s ago is
never swept; the sweep is bounded by max_candidates_per_run; a crash-simulated PENDING task
whose directory is gone converges to DONE; the sweep never raises out of run_once (one bad
repo must not kill the loop).
acceptance_criteria: Loop follows the maintenance.py/queue_loop.py shape (daemon thread, stop Event, run_once, start/stop/is_alive) and is started in server_http.py only when its config flag is enabled
run_once() is callable via MCP with the loop disabled
An orphan is not actioned on first sighting; it requires orphan_confirm_runs consecutive sightings and orphan_min_age_seconds
A worktree created seconds ago is never swept
The sweep is bounded by max_candidates_per_run and a wall-clock budget, and never holds a lock across the whole sweep
A PENDING task whose directory vanished converges to CLEANUP_DONE
run_once never raises: one unreadable repo does not kill the loop

notes: Periodic sweep: daemon thread + stop Event + run_once + start/stop/is_alive/status, started in server_http only behind sweep_enabled (default off); run_once callable via MCP with the loop off. Orphans need N consecutive sightings AND a min age. Bounded by candidate count and wall clock. No sweep-wide lock. Fixed two real bugs found by their own tests: the claimed-set missed still-RUNNING tasks, and the converge half passed no probes so it was inert in production.

items.title: Worktree Janitor P4: multi-node execution at the owning node-agent
items.description:
Multi-node: execution happens at the owning node-agent. The controller never removes
a remote path.

This mirrors exactly what /v1/repo/{op} and /v1/repo-evidence already do for reads: the
controller cannot see another node's filesystem, so it must ask the node that owns it.

Node-agent (node_agent.py): add authenticated routes
  GET  /v1/worktree/candidates?repo_path=...   -> classification report for THIS node
  POST /v1/worktree/cleanup                    -> body {repo_path, worktree_path,
                                                   expected_head, expected_branch}

items.title: Worktree Janitor P6: disk-pressure escalation (per-mount) + scratch/cache policy
items.description:
Disk-pressure escalation, and a durable policy for scratch/cache locations.

Escalation (must obey I7): when free space on the filesystem holding the candidates crosses
configured thresholds, the janitor may ONLY:
  (a) shorten grace_seconds toward grace_floor_seconds (never below),
  (b) reorder AUTO_SAFE candidates largest-first,
  (c) raise log/alert severity and emit a WORKTREE_CLEANUP_PRESSURE event.
It may NEVER: downgrade or skip a predicate, promote REVIEW/BLOCKED to AUTO_SAFE, pass
force, or touch a dirty/unmerged tree. A test must assert that at 99% full a dirty worktree
is still not removed.

Measurement: reuse host_metrics (already collects disk usage) rather than a second
implementation. Thresholds are per-mount, because the audited reality on m910 is that the
pressure is NOT where the worktrees are: /dev/sda3 (worktrees, /home) was 26% used with 83G
free while tmpfs /tmp was 74% used and had already hit an EDQUOT that broke tooling. So:
- Evaluate pressure on the filesystem of each candidate path, never a global number.
- Removing worktrees frees the worktree filesystem only; state that explicitly in the
  report so an operator is not misled into thinking it relieves /tmp.

Scratch/cache policy (the second half of the audited problem): /tmp is a 7.6G RAM-backed
tmpfs with usrquota, and per-user quota exhaustion there breaks unrelated tooling. Propose
and document (in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md) a policy for where agent scratch/logs/caches live,
with a recommendation to place durable scratch on the ext4 root rather than tmpfs, plus a
bounded retention sweep for whatever location is chosen. Implement only the retention sweep
for directories the project itself owns; do NOT touch another tool's directories.

DoD: tests for threshold behaviour including the 99%-full dirty-worktree refusal; per-mount
evaluation (a candidate on a roomy mount is not escalated because another mount is full);
the report explicitly names which filesystem the reclaim affects; retention sweep is bounded
and dry-run by default.
acceptance_criteria: Escalation may only shorten grace toward grace_floor_seconds, reorder largest-first, and raise alert severity
A test asserts that at 99% full a dirty or unmerged worktree is still refused, and that force is never enabled
Pressure is evaluated per-mount on the candidate's own filesystem, reusing host_metrics; a candidate on a roomy mount is not escalated because another mount is full
The report states explicitly which filesystem a reclaim affects, so removing worktrees is not mistaken for relieving tmpfs /tmp
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md records the scratch/cache location policy including the tmpfs-quota finding and the recommendation to keep durable scratch off RAM-backed tmpfs
Any retention sweep is bounded, dry-run by default, and touches only directories this project owns

items.title: Prompt delivery/acceptance gate: enforce across supervisor2 + MCP send tools, then promote advisory->enforce
items.description:
Finish wiring the PROMPT DELIVERY / ACCEPTANCE GATE into the two send paths that still decide
for themselves, and promote the gate from advisory to enforce.

Already shipped on branch feat/prompt-delivery-gate (advisory default, zero behaviour change):
terminal_mcp/delivery_gate.py (the pure decision point), config.PromptDeliveryConfig +
_load_prompt_delivery_config, queue_engine._dispatch wired through it,
queue_store.record_delivery_verdict, the contract in docs/prompt-submission.md ("The acceptance
gate") and a pointer in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md section 5, plus tests/test_delivery_gate.py.
This item is the REMAINDER, deliberately not guessed at.

THE RULE (source of truth: docs/prompt-submission.md "The acceptance gate"): a prompt is
DELIVERED only when BOTH (1) the send receipt's delivery_state is SUBMIT_CONFIRMED, AND (2) a
separate post-submit observation shows the target actually took it. SUBMIT_CONFIRMED alone
proves Enter was processed, not that the agent read the prompt and started.

1. supervisor2.execute_send. It currently does: if submit_status == "SUBMIT_UNCONFIRMED" ->
   cas_update(state=blocked, stop_reason=submit_unconfirmed) + block_policy; else ->
   cas_update(state=observing). That is the same denylist shape queue_engine had -- a TEXT_SENT
   receipt, or any delivery_state added to adapters.py later, falls through to observing.
   Replace with delivery_gate.evaluate. The care needed:
   - The action state machine is a CAS chain (approved -> sent -> observing|blocked|failed) and
     the row is CAS'd to sent BEFORE the send. Do NOT change that ordering: it is what makes a
     duplicate execute_send a no-op.
   - A NOT_ACCEPTED verdict needs its OWN stop_reason (proposed: acceptance_not_observed) and
     must not be conflated with submit_unconfirmed. They call for different operator action:
     submit_unconfirmed means the submit itself is unproven, acceptance_not_observed means the
     submit is confirmed but the agent has not visibly started. Conflating them would tell an
     operator to retry something that must never be retried.
   - DECIDE and document: should NOT_ACCEPTED call block_policy (pausing the whole watch) or
     only block the single action? Blocking the whole policy because one agent was slow to start
     is probably too aggressive; blocking only the action risks the chain advancing. Pick one
     with a stated rationale.

2. Direct MCP send tools (terminal_send_text, terminal_send_bound and the _bound variants).
   These return a receipt and the CALLER decides, so in-process enforcement is impossible --
   for an external caller the docs section IS the rule. What is possible and additive: return
   the verdict as a receipt field (proposed name: delivery_verdict) alongside the existing
   submission_id / evidence / stage that core.py's _enrich_receipt already adds, so a caller
   branches on one field instead of re-deriving the rule.
   - DECIDE: compute it inline on every send (costs one extra status read of latency per send)
     or only when the caller opts in via a parameter. Measure before choosing.
   - _enrich_receipt already emits stage=ACCEPTANCE for the enter-sent-but-unconfirmed case.
     Reconcile the two vocabularies rather than introducing a third overlapping one.

3. Promotion advisory -> enforce. Run advisory in production for a defined window, export the
   recorded metadata.delivery_verdict distribution, and confirm there are no false negatives
   (NOT_ACCEPTED returned for a task that had genuinely started) -- a false negative stalls real
   work, which is worse than the fail-open it replaces. Only then flip prompt_delivery.mode to
   enforce, per-deployment, with an explicit human go-ahead, the same discipline the per-lane
   auto_dispatch_enabled decision documents. Record the observed false-negative rate in
   docs/REQUIREMENTS.md BEFORE flipping.

4. Dashboard surface: show the verdict (kind, activation, acceptance, evidence) on a held task
   so an operator can see WHY it is held rather than just that it is. tests/test_dashboard.py's
   pinned route inventory is authoritative -- update it deliberately if a route is added.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no new queue status (DISPATCH_UNCERTAIN already carries the
held-after-confirmed-submit case); no schema migration (the verdict lives in the existing
metadata JSON column, bounded to 5 history entries); no change to the bounded Escape+Enter
activation retry, which stays owned by core.py under its own evidence gate; no automatic resend
on NOT_ACCEPTED, ever -- the submit is confirmed, so a resend duplicates it.

CLAUDE-SPECIFIC RULE that must survive any refactor here: never raw/repeated Enter. If a prompt
is still in the input box, inspect via terminal_input_context, clear it, then exactly one
terminal_send_text(..., press_enter=True). No bare terminal_send_keys(["Enter"]) to help it
along, no second Enter because the first looked slow.
acceptance_criteria: supervisor2.execute_send routes through delivery_gate.evaluate with a positive allowlist; a TEXT_SENT or unrecognised delivery_state no longer reaches state=observing
NOT_ACCEPTED has its own stop_reason distinct from submit_unconfirmed, and the decision on whether it blocks the policy or only the action is documented with rationale
The CAS ordering (approved -> sent before the send) is unchanged, and a duplicate execute_send is still refused
terminal_send_text/_bound expose the verdict as an additive receipt field reconciled with the existing stage=ACCEPTANCE vocabulary; no existing field changes meaning
Advisory-mode verdict distribution from a real production window is recorded in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, including the observed false-negative rate, BEFORE any enforce flip
prompt_delivery.mode=enforce is flipped only per-deployment with an explicit human go-ahead
Dashboard shows kind/activation/acceptance/evidence for a held task; the pinned route inventory is updated deliberately if a route is added
Regression tests for supervisor2: TEXT_SENT does not reach observing, NOT_ACCEPTED blocks with its own reason, duplicate send still refused
No new queue status and no schema migration introduced

items.title: Scheduler: auto-refill idle workers and reclaim stalled sessions
items.description:
Scheduling is not work-conserving: READY backlog work coexists with genuinely idle compatible workers and nothing dispatches, so capacity is wasted and stale sessions hold worker slots indefinitely.

OBSERVED (production, 2026-09-14):
- supervisor loop running every 20s, but supervisor_status: watch_count=4, enabled_watch_count=0, stalled_count=2 -- i.e. zero enabled watches despite live workers.
- watches stop silently via max_iterations_exceeded / manual_unwatch / target_missing, removing scheduling visibility from workers that are still alive.
- linux1 finished implementation+tests and sits at an empty prompt.
- hp3-work reported done and sits at an empty prompt.
- hp1 stale ~35h, never reclaimed, still occupying a worker slot.
- linux2/hp2 had ~1h-old activity while the UI still rendered composing/imagining.

SCOPE:
1. Worker state model distinguishing RUNNING, IDLE_READY, WAITING_INPUT, STALLED, BLOCKED, UNAVAILABLE/OFFLINE, RESERVED, UNKNOWN. Empty prompt after completion becomes IDLE_READY after a configurable 30-60s debounce. UNKNOWN must be re-probed, never permanent.
2. Refill invariant: ready_compatible_tasks>0 && idle_compatible_workers>0 must not persist beyond a configurable refill SLA (default <=60s) without a persisted reason code (DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED, CAPABILITY_MISMATCH, RESERVED_FOR_HOTFIX, NODE_OFFLINE, CONCURRENCY_LIMIT, WORKTREE_CONFLICT, PERMISSION_DENIED).
3. Watch lifecycle robustness: max_iterations_exceeded must not permanently remove worker coverage; target_missing must trigger rediscovery/reconciliation; manual unwatch stays respected but is recorded as intentional exclusion; supervisor restart rebuilds observation idempotently from persisted sessions.
4. Stalled reclaim on MULTIPLE signals (tmux activity age, prompt state, output hash/no-progress, running child process, pending shell command, submit/activation state). Probe before reclaim; never reclaim on one weak signal; preserve a genuinely running child command; release lease exactly once with audit trail.
5. Dispatch safety: capability matching preserved; no two tasks into one tmux session; delivery incomplete until SUBMIT_CONFIRMED/activation evidence; unconfirmed send returns task to READY without leaking a worker reservation; compare-and-swap/lease prevents double-claim.
6. Observability: usable worker count, RUNNING/IDLE_READY/STALLED/BLOCKED/OFFLINE counts, READY task count, compatible-ready per worker, utilization %, idle-with-ready-work duration, last dispatch timestamp, non-dispatch reason, reclaimed count. The dashboard must make it obvious WHY a worker is idle.

DEPENDENCIES:
- blg_orch_no_workers_declared (IN_PROGRESS): capability_profiles has 0 rows, so pm_router returns NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER for everything. Capability-routed refill cannot find candidates until profiles exist; refill must still work for non-capability-routed dispatch and must report CAPABILITY_MISMATCH as an explicit reason rather than failing silently.
- Composes with blg_orch_scheduler (P1 cross-project portfolio scheduling) and blg_967d4e3aa293 (P3 deterministic portfolio scheduler); this item is single-project work-conservation and must not pre-empt their allocation model.
- Interacts with blg_39f82cd2fe3a (prompt delivery/acceptance gate) for SUBMIT_CONFIRMED.
acceptance_criteria: With >=3 idle compatible workers and >=3 independent READY tasks, every eligible worker is filled automatically in one refill pass with no manual sends
READY-compatible-work + IDLE-compatible-worker never persists >60s without an explicit persisted reason code
max_iterations_exceeded does not permanently remove scheduling visibility from a live worker
target_missing then reappearing reconciles the worker back into coverage
A stale-looking session with a genuinely running child process is NOT reclaimed
A confidently stalled session is marked STALLED and its lease released exactly once, with audit trail
Concurrent scheduler passes cannot double-claim the same task or worker
Unconfirmed/rejected prompt delivery returns the task to READY and leaks no worker reservation
Restart/recovery of observation is idempotent
Existing supervisor v1/v2 and dashboard tests remain green; changes are additive
Before/after utilization evidence reported

notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: supervisor.py disables watches for 7 reasons and called set_enabled(...,True) from NOWHERE in the codebase -- every disable was permanent. A watch that hit max_iterations while its worker kept working never came back, so live workers lost scheduling visibility forever. That is exactly watch_count=4/enabled=0.

PHASE 1 COMMITTED: branch fix/scheduler-refill @ 02efdf5 (NOT merged, NOT deployed).
  terminal_mcp/scheduler_health.py (new): worker state model (RUNNING/IDLE_READY/WAITING_INPUT/STALLED/BLOCKED/OFFLINE/RESERVED/UNKNOWN), multi-signal classify_worker with configurable idle debounce, may_reclaim requiring STALLED+high confidence, watch_recovery_action, evaluate_refill with reason codes, utilization_snapshot.
  terminal_mcp/supervisor.py: reconcile_watches() + _target_alive() + store.reenable_watch/reset_iterations/note_reconcile_attempt, reconcile_attempts column, watch_reconciled event, enriched status (disabled/recoverable/intentional counts + per-watch reasons).
  tests: test_scheduler_health.py (35), test_supervisor_reconcile.py (9). Regression 227 passed.

BEFORE/AFTER on a COPY of the real supervisor.db (production not mutated):
  BEFORE enabled=0/4 (recoverable=3, intentional=1)
  AFTER  enabled=2/4 -- restored mcp-work + terminal-mcp-main (max_iterations_exceeded); left mesflow-dell (manual_unwatch, deliberate) and wtest (target still missing).

STILL OPEN (phase 2): the dispatch side. evaluate_refill decides and explains but nothing yet claims a lease, sends a prompt under the SUBMIT_CONFIRMED contract, or reclaims a STALLED session. Needs wiring into queue_engine's dispatch path; deserves its own review.

Integrated into main. Closing this also required fixing backlog_service.complete(), which raised AttributeError on this very item because its evidence field was a plain string rather than a dict -- the ledger could not close its own row. Original evidence text preserved as a note.
